elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Section 6.11 as rendered: "Such examinations may not ... (b) be conducted more than once in any twelve (12) month period" — the previously redacted period is fixed at twelve months.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: The inserted notice is "upon at least fifteen (15) days' prior written notice", which is the fallback period, not the preferred 30 days.
Section 6.11 contains no temporal restriction on when the examination may be conducted; the only bracketed limits at (a) and (c) remain redacted and cannot be read as a business-hours condition.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: Retained language: "an independent public accounting firm of nationally recognized standing designated by Harpoon and reasonably acceptable to AbbVie".

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Section 6.11 only limits what the firm may disclose to Harpoon ("only whether the reports are correct or not ... No other information shall be shared"); Section 6.13's confidentiality-agreement requirement runs to the "Audit Expert" appointed under Section 6.12, not to the Section 6.11 auditing firm, so no express confidentiality obligation binds the auditor.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: No off-site or remote-review language appears anywhere in Section 6.11 as rendered; the drafter expressly declined to pursue this preferred item.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Rendered cost trigger is "an underpayment of more than ten percent (10%) of the reported amounts", above the preferred 5% threshold.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: Section 6.11 grants access only to "the books and records maintained pursuant to this Section 6.11" and contains no express system-access grant or prohibition; the redacted items (a)/(c) prevent a definitive reading, and no express "no access to Customer systems" covenant was added.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: "Such examinations may not ... (b) be conducted more than once in any twelve (12) month period" — an annual cap on the face of the clause.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: "At the request of Harpoon, upon at least fifteen (15) days' prior written notice, AbbVie shall permit ..." replaces the prior on-request-with-no-notice trigger.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: "the cost of this audit shall be borne by Harpoon, unless the audit reveals an underpayment of more than ten percent (10%) of the reported amounts, in which case AbbVie shall bear the cost" — the open-ended "variance [***] ... or [***]" trigger is replaced by a single 10% underpayment test.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback: all three fallback elements (annual frequency cap, 15 days' prior written notice, Vendor-borne cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%) are established in operative language in Section 6.11, not merely promised in the comment.

Preferred level is not reached: notice is 15 rather than 30 days, the cost trigger is 10% rather than 5%, and business-hours, off-site-where-possible, express auditor confidentiality and no-system-access terms are absent. That is acceptable because the fallback checklist is complete, but the drafter should not represent this as the preferred position.

Minimality holds. Each of the three edits sits inside the existing sentence structure of Section 6.11; the notice phrase is inserted into the existing request trigger, the redacted frequency period is filled with "twelve (12) month", and the cost trigger is rewritten. Deleting the alternative "or [***]" cost-shift trigger is necessary rather than cosmetic: leaving a second, undefined trigger would let Vendor shift audit cost to us outside the 10% underpayment test and would leave the element dependent on an undefined trigger. No survival tails, expense language, procedures or extraneous requirements were added.

Intent is preserved. The independent-auditor designation, the reasonable-acceptability approval right, the disclosure limitation ("only whether the reports are correct or not ... No other information shall be shared"), the redacted limits at (a) and (c) with the prior-underpayment exception, and Sections 6.12-6.13 all survive unchanged and without contradiction.

Residual point worth noting to the drafter (not a defect in the fallback): the retained opener "Except as provided below" plus Section 6.12 lets the Audit Expert reallocate "the costs of such determination as well as the initial audit" in a dispute. That is pre-existing language and only operates on dispute, so it does not defeat the default cost rule, but if the counterparty pushes back it is the mechanism by which our 10% allocation can be displaced.

If a second pass is available, the cheapest incremental upgrades toward the preferred position are: (i) add "during AbbVie's normal business hours" after "prior written notice"; and (ii) add an express confidentiality obligation on the Section 6.11 accounting firm (Section 6.13 currently binds only the Audit Expert).
